name: Occupied Threshold

stars.name: Dominion's Eye
stars.notes: An older yellow-orange star whose steady output has supported habitable conditions for billions of years. Its colloquial name was imposed by the Kethrani Ascendancy after the 2711 occupation—the original colonial name, 'Hearthlight,' is used only by the resistance.

planets.name: Slag
planets.notes: Molten inner world with no strategic value. The Kethrani use its gravitational well for execution disposal—condemned prisoners' remains are launched into decaying orbits around this world.

planets.name: Threshold
planets.notes: The system's primary world and the seat of occupation. Formerly a prosperous agricultural colony, now under martial law. The Kethrani garrison controls the cities; the resistance holds the mountains and deep forests.

planets.name: Outerhold
planets.notes: A colder, drier habitable world with smaller settlements. The Kethrani occupation is lighter here—fewer troops, less infrastructure—but the population is no less resentful. Underground supply networks connect resistance cells across both worlds.

planets.name: The Yard
planets.notes: Airless rocky world converted into a Kethrani military depot. Surface hangars house occupation support vehicles, ammunition stores, and a prisoner-of-war camp holding approximately 4,000 resistance fighters.

planets.name: Watcher
planets.notes: Standard hydrogen-helium giant. The Kethrani maintain a fuel-harvesting operation in its upper atmosphere and have fortified three moons as naval bases controlling system access.

planets.name: Exile's End
planets.notes: Frozen outer world. Resistance intelligence believes the Kethrani are constructing a deep-space communications relay here, potentially linking the occupation to Ascendancy core worlds.

anomalies.name: The Pyre Field
anomalies.notes: Wreckage of the original colonial defense fleet, destroyed in the opening hours of the 2711 invasion. The Kethrani leave it in orbit as a deliberate psychological weapon—a reminder of the cost of resistance.

anomalies.name: Signal Ghost
anomalies.notes: Intermittent encrypted transmissions detected from the outer system. The Kethrani claim they originate from malfunctioning pre-occupation satellites. Resistance intelligence believes they are communications from an external liberation fleet.

asteroid_belts.name: Hearthstone Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Rich metallic belt being strip-mined by the Kethrani to supply their occupation infrastructure. Pre-occupation mining cooperatives have been dissolved and their assets seized.

stations.name: Ascendancy Command
stations.notes: Kethrani occupation headquarters. Houses the military governor's office, intelligence operations, and an orbital weapons platform capable of precision strikes anywhere on Threshold's surface.

stations.name: The Processing Center
stations.notes: Orbital detention and interrogation facility. Suspected resistance members are brought here for processing. Survivors describe conditions designed to break psychological resistance through isolation and sensory deprivation.

stations.name: Hearth Station
stations.notes: Former civilian spaceport now controlled by Kethrani customs. All incoming and outgoing traffic is searched. Smuggling supplies to the resistance through this chokepoint requires extraordinary measures.

faction_control.notes: The Kethrani invaded in 2711 and have maintained occupation for fifteen years. The original colonial government operates in exile. A persistent resistance movement on both inhabited worlds conducts sabotage, intelligence gathering, and occasional direct assaults on occupation forces. The Kethrani response has been increasingly brutal.

history: Occupied Threshold was originally named the Hearthlight System, colonized in 2534 as an agricultural settlement. For 177 years it was unremarkable—a productive, peaceful colony exporting foodstuffs to neighboring systems.

The Kethrani Ascendancy invaded in 2711 as part of a broader territorial expansion campaign. The colonial defense fleet was destroyed in hours. The ground campaign lasted three months before the colonial government surrendered to prevent further civilian casualties. The government-in-exile formed within weeks.

Fifteen years of occupation have hardened both sides. The resistance has grown from scattered saboteurs to a coordinated insurgency with supply lines, intelligence networks, and cells on both inhabited worlds. The Kethrani have responded with collective punishment, orbital detention facilities, and the public execution of captured resistance leaders. External powers express concern but take no action.
description: Occupied Threshold is a system under a boot. Its yellow-orange star shines on two habitable worlds that were, until fifteen years ago, quiet agricultural colonies. Now the orbital space around Threshold is cluttered with the wreckage of the old defense fleet—left deliberately by the Kethrani as a monument to futility—and the surface below is carved into occupation zones, curfew districts, and restricted areas. Outerhold endures a lighter but no less resented military presence. The Yard, the airless fourth world, has been converted into a depot and prison camp.

The occupation is stable but not secure. The Kethrani control the cities, the orbitals, and the space lanes, but they do not control the mountains, the forests, or the hearts of the population. The resistance operates with increasing sophistication, disrupting supply lines, assassinating collaborators, and maintaining encrypted communications with the government-in-exile. The Kethrani response—mass detention, orbital surveillance, collective punishment—generates more recruits than it eliminates. Intelligence analysts describe a system approaching a tipping point.

For outsiders, Occupied Threshold presents a moral and practical calculus. The resistance desperately needs weapons, medical supplies, and communications equipment, and pays well for smugglers who can bypass Kethrani customs. The Kethrani themselves hire contractors for infrastructure security and counterinsurgency support. Journalists who enter the system rarely leave with the story the Kethrani want told. And the Signal Ghost in the outer system—those encrypted transmissions that may or may not herald an approaching liberation fleet—keeps everyone guessing.
